facts.citation: Y. S. Shao et al., "Simba: Scaling Deep-Learning Inference with Multi-Chip-Module-Based Architecture", MICRO-52, 2019.

mac.quote: "Each chip has a peak performance of 4 tera-ops per second (TOPS) using 8-bit weights and activations and 24-bit accumulation."
mac.note: timeloop-accelergy-exercises ships PEAccuBuffer at datawidth 24 but mac.adder_width 16 -- accumulator storage at the published width and accumulator arithmetic at another. 24 is used for both.

GlobalBuffer.declared_claim: Carries Outputs at 8b, BELOW the 24b accumulator, and says so in the YAML with a `# psum-width-ok:` note: the PE post-processing unit requantizes on the way out of PEAccuBuffer, so this level holds activations rather than partial sums.
GlobalBuffer.not_verified: The buffer and PE geometries below the MAC come from the exercises repo, not from a table checked against the paper. They are a REPRODUCTION, not a citation. Only the precisions above have been traced to the paper.

deviation.technology: Simba is a TSMC 16nm FinFET design modelled here at 45nm, the largest node deviation in the study. Not corrected: correcting one design would reintroduce the mixed-node confound the standard removes.

mapper_settings.seed_note: timeloop-mapper v4 exposes no random seed; pytimeloop's Mapper spec has no `random_seed` attribute. ECC_MAPPER_SEED is RECORDED so a result says which value was asked for, but it does not make the search deterministic. What does bound it is the thread count and victory condition, both of which are in the fingerprint -- so pin ECC_MAPPER_THREADS for a reproducible run rather than leaving it at 'all cores', which differs per machine.
